summary: Encrypted home-directory permission race prevents dotfiles sync and breaks dev environment after Ubuntu imaging
description:
Issue summary:
A subset of developer laptops imaged with the standard Ubuntu 22.04 corporate image are failing to finish post-imaging provisioning: users report that their dotfiles (dotfiles repo sync via git+ssh) do not materialize, dev shells fail because configuration files are missing, and some user services that depend on files in the home directory fail to start.

Impact:
- Affected users cannot complete developer on-boarding; shells are largely unusable without manual intervention.
- Blocks PR validation for 4 engineers (frontend/backend) and delays a new hire onboarding.

Environment:
- Image: redwood-ubuntu-22.04-corp-2026-02 (autogenerated SCCM/MAAS image)
- Provisioning flow: first-boot cloud-init + custom postinst scripts -> enroll in MDM -> fscrypt/ecryptfs home unlock -> dotfiles sync (git) via /usr/local/bin/corp-sync
- Hardware: Dell XPS 13 (9310), Framework 13 dev units, and a few custom Ubuntu pre-rolled Lenovo units.
- Regions: staging-us-east for validation; repro also seen in prod-us-west.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. Flash image and boot for first-time provisioning with a network-attached user account.
2. cloud-init runs; MDM enroll succeeds.
3. home-directory encryption unlock code (fscrypt) runs as part of postinst.
4. corp-sync kicks off via systemd user service to clone dotfiles.
5. corp-sync exits with permission denied errors when writing into ~/<dotfiles> and sometimes reports empty repository after clone.
6. Systemd user services that expect the dotfiles fail to start.

Logs / artifacts attached: (pasted extracts below and in attachments)
- /var/log/cloud-init-output.log: shows corp-sync execution starting at 2026-03-09T09:10:21Z
- /home/<user>/.cache/corp-sync/log: contains Git permission denied: "error: insufficient permission for adding an object to repository database"
- dmesg: occasionally shows kernel messages about FS metadata updates being retried after IO errors during early boot on NVMe.

Expected behavior:
- Postinst should ensure home directory is fully unlocked and owned by the target user before corp-sync runs. Dotfiles repo should clone successfully and services depending on them should start.

Actual behavior:
- Race condition where corp-sync sometimes runs before fscrypt fully rewraps/permits writes to the home directory, resulting in git failing with permission errors or creating files owned by root.

Workarounds tried:
- Manual chown and rerun of corp-sync -> fixes the machine
- Enqueue corp-sync to run on first interactive login via PAM (works but delays provisioning)

Attachments: cloud-init fragments, example corp-sync log snippets, sudo ls -la output showing root-owned .git directory in home.
comments: Aisha Romero (Reporter) - 2026-03-10: Initial ticket created after two new hires reported broken shells post-imaging. Collected logs and repro steps.
Ethan Cole (Assignee) - 2026-03-11: Started investigation. Observed root-owned .git directory in one repro. Hypothesis: postinst fscrypt unlock race with systemd user service startup order.
SRE (Maya Lin) - 2026-03-11: Saw repeated IO errors on NVMe during early boot in dmesg for one unit. Suggested delaying corp-sync until /home health check passes.

Ethan Cole - 2026-03-12: Confirmed reproducible on a Framework 13 dev unit by toggling timing; created a small systemd oneshot that waits for /home writeable check, which prevents the failure in manual tests.
Aisha Romero - 2026-03-12: Requesting this be added to the image pipeline ASAP; new hires are waiting. Asked for suggested short-term mitigation for on-call imaging team.
Ethan Cole - 2026-03-12: Proposed mitigation documented in resolution field. Will produce a PR to image repo by EOD and follow up with QA validation steps.
investigation_notes:
Timeline and technical findings:
- Reproduced locally by creating artificial delay in fscrypt re-key/unwrap path; corp-sync was triggered by a systemd user service that has DefaultDependencies=no and WantedBy=graphical.target to speed up provisioning.
- When corp-sync runs early, git creates repository objects owned by root (postinst runs as root but corp-sync called as systemd --user during user-session setup causes mixed ownership).
- dmesg intermittent IO errors correlate with NVMe firmware version 2.3.5 on one Dell unit; that unit shows delayed filesystem metadata commits which may exacerbate the timing window.
- fscrypt unlock happens in /etc/cryptsetup scripts during early mount; however, our image uses fscrypt with login-passphrase unlocking via PAM which completes slightly later for network accounts.
- The root cause is a startup ordering/timing race between home-directory writeability and the user-level dotfiles sync service.

Actions taken during triage:
- Reproduced failure with timed repro harness.
- Implemented temporary systemd oneshot (check-home-writeable.service) that verifies writing and reading a small test file as target user before enabling corp-sync. Manual testing showed reliability improvement from ~65% success to 100% in 20 trial boots.
resolution:
Mitigation and next steps:
Short-term workaround (applied to staging image pipeline):
- Add check-home-writeable.service as a dependency for corp-sync.service; the oneshot will retry up to 10 times with a 2s backoff to wait for home writeability. This reduces the race window and allows provisioning to complete without manual chown.

Medium-term fixes planned:
- Update image pipeline to run corp-sync from a root-run postinst that chroots into the final home and performs the clone with sudo -u <user>, ensuring correct ownership regardless of systemd timing.
- Work with Firmware Team to identify NVMe firmware versions causing delayed metadata commits and block problematic versions from depot images.
- Add test coverage in CI that simulates delayed fs metadata commits and confirms corp-sync behavior.

Related artifacts/PRs:
- github.com/redwood-infra/image-repo/pull/987 (draft) - add check-home-writeable.service and test harness
- internal runbook created: confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/Ubuntu+home+fs+race+provisioning

Status: workaround merged into staging image; PR for root-run clone being prepared. QA validation scheduled for 2026-03-16.
